title: A bounded buffer on one monitor

blocks.text: The page's `ProducerConsumerMonitor` coordinates a producer and a consumer on one monitor: each waits with `wait()` **in a loop** while it cannot go on, because a thread that wakes up may find the condition false again. The page wakes the other side with `notifyAll()`, and it warns never to swallow an `InterruptedException`.
Write `BoundedBuffer<T>`, a first-in, first-out buffer of at most `capacity` items, on one monitor:

items: `void put(T item)` adds an item, **waiting while the buffer is full**.
`T take()` removes and returns the oldest item, **waiting while it is empty**.
`int size()` is the number of items held.
A thread interrupted while it waits in `put` or `take` leaves with the `InterruptedException`.

rows: empty: another thread's `take()`, then that thread is interrupted
empty: two other threads each call `take()`, then `put("z")`
one of them returns `"z"`; the other keeps waiting

cases.says: An item put into the buffer is the item taken out, and size follows.
Items are taken in the order they were put.
put on a full buffer waits until a take makes room.
take on an empty buffer waits until a put brings an item.
A take that is waiting ends with InterruptedException when its thread is interrupted, instead of swallowing it.
Two takers wait on an empty buffer and one item arrives: one taker gets it and the other checks again and goes back to waiting, instead of returning with nothing.

concepts: An InterruptedException must not be swallowed: it is passed on, or the interrupt flag is restored.
wait() releases the monitor and is called in a loop over its condition, because a woken thread may find the condition false again.
